    Changelog

    distmer 0.9.0.9000

    Versioning reset before the first stable release

    • The active package version is now 0.9.0.9000: a pre-release development line leading to the first stable 1.0.0 release.
    • Earlier version-like numbers were internal implementation checkpoints, not published package releases. Their detailed notes remain below for audit traceability but are explicitly labelled as unreleased checkpoints.
    • Four-component .9000 versions are development snapshots. The public release will use 1.0.0, with later releases following semantic versioning.

    The source previously carrying the internal 2.9.1.9000 label was renumbered to 0.9.0.9000; this is a version-policy correction, not a rollback of code or validated capability.

    Mixed-covariate and asymptotic-inference hardening

    • Rebuilt the documentation as a seven-guide ecological workflow: an explicit distance-based mixed-model introduction, fixed effects, pairwise contrasts, distance and dispersion diagnostics, unbalanced designs, random effects, and reproducible validation. Worked examples now use vegan::dune, vegan::mite, and vegan::pyrifos, with ggplot2 figures. Implementation routing is kept as a secondary reference in the random-effects guide.

    • Mixed and nested covariate projectors now use scale-aware stratum projection, so structurally zero between/within components cannot acquire numerical rank. Single-random-intercept models assign a numeric term that is constant within groups to the between-group stratum. Nested covariate inference rejects a numeric term with no deepest-stratum variation because that higher-level term requires a denominator outside the supported envelope.

    • Nested covariate Type I/II/III hypotheses now apply to covariate main effects and slope interactions as well as factors. Their Freedman–Lane reduced model retains every term used to adjust the observed numerator.

    • Balanced random-intercept inference now honours Type I/II/III fixed-effect hypotheses instead of coupling the numerator partition to the random-effect denominator choice.

    • P(MC) now derives its eigenvalue spectrum from each test’s orthogonal numerator-plus-denominator stratum. Variation outside that stratum can no longer change an upper-level mixed-model p-value.

    • permanova_mixed_covariate(permutations = "all") now enumerates the actual whole-group or within-group action, respects max_exact, and reports its finite attainable space.

    • Continuous random-slope sign-flip inference remains available with unequal covariate information. The parametric F(1, ng - 1) reference is now limited to rank-one Euclidean slopes with equal within-group SSx; the slope variance component subtracts MS[Residual] * mean(1 / SSx).

    • The source release audit scans all Rd files and the current seven-vignette series. Development handoff and readiness documents now follow the active version rather than the retired Phase 28 tree.

    Internal checkpoint label: 2.9.0.9000 (unreleased).

    Type I / II / III sums of squares for the fixed part of mixed designs

    • The type argument of permanova() now applies to the covariate-adjusted mixed engines, not only pure fixed-effect models. permanova_mixed_covariate() and permanova_nested_covariate() gained a hypothesis argument ("I" sequential, "II" marginal/containment-respecting, "III" partial), threaded from the front-door type. The sum-of-squares type changes only how each fixed term’s numerator reduced model is formed; the random-structure denominator is unchanged. Types coincide for an orthogonal balanced fixed structure and differ only when the fixed terms are non-orthogonal (crossed factors with unequal cell counts). Validated against car::Anova: for a block design with an unbalanced within-block A*B structure, distmer reproduces the Type I, Type II, and (through the front door’s automatic sum-to-zero contrasts) Type III F ratios exactly. The front door no longer warns that type is ignored for these engines.

    Internal checkpoint label: 2.8.0.9000 (unreleased).

    Covariate adjustment for single random-intercept designs (split-plot / RCB ANCOVA)

    • permanova(distance ~ factor + covariate + (1 | group)) now routes to a new engine, permanova_mixed_covariate(), extending covariate adjustment beyond the balanced nested engine to the single-random-intercept case. Each fixed term is classified by whether it varies within the grouping unit: between-unit (whole-plot) factors are tested over the between-group random-intercept stratum, while within-unit terms – sub-plot or randomized-block factors, observation-level covariates, and covariate-by-factor slope interactions – are tested over the within-group residual. This is the distance-based split-plot and randomized-block analysis of covariance. Unlike permanova_nested_covariate(), it removes the covariate’s between-unit component from the factor denominator and adjusts each whole-plot factor for the covariate’s between-unit slope (which differs from the pooled slope), so a covariate with between-unit structure is handled correctly without a manual decompose_covariate() step. Validated to reproduce the whole-plot factor test against aov(y ~ covariate + factor + Error(group)) and the within-unit (sub-plot factor, covariate, slopes) tests against the corresponding blocked linear model, exactly, including degrees of freedom.

    Internal checkpoint label: 2.7.0.9000 (unreleased).

    Continuous-covariate random slopes

    • permanova(distance ~ x + (1 + x | group)) with a numeric x now routes to a new engine, permanova_random_slope_continuous(), for the covariate-by- random model of Anderson, Gorley & Clarke (2008, Fig. 1.48b). The fixed slope has no exact single-source denominator in the full observation space (its expected mean square mixes the random-slope and residual components with different coefficients), so the test aggregates – exactly as the two-level categorical engine reduces to per-subject difference vectors – to one within-group slope vector per group, then tests the equally weighted mean slope against the between-group slope variation by whole-group sign flips, with a parametric F(1, ng - 1) p-value for Euclidean dissimilarities. For a balanced design this is the exact two-stage slope test, validated to reproduce it to machine precision and to agree closely with lmerTest. The earlier attempt to build this denominator with structured_denominator() was abandoned: the differing expected-mean-square coefficients inflated the synthesised denominator and pushed the pseudo-F ~1.6x below both gold standards, whereas the aggregated slope-vector test matches them exactly.
    • permanova_random_slope() (the balanced two-level categorical sign-flip engine) now rejects a continuous slope variable with a message pointing to the continuous engine, instead of failing obscurely.

    Internal checkpoint label: 2.6.0.9000 (unreleased).

    Monte-Carlo asymptotic p-value: P(MC)

    • permanova() now reports P(MC) alongside P(perm) for designs tested in the full observation space (fixed, balanced mixed, nested, crossed, hybrid). Following McArdle & Anderson (2001) and Anderson & Robinson (2003), the numerator and denominator sums of squares are drawn from the eigenvalue- weighted chi-square distribution implied by the Gower matrix, so the p-value stays smooth when the true permutation space is tiny – the usual situation for the upper strata of a mixed design, where restricted permutation yields very few unique arrangements. It reduces exactly to the classical F distribution in the univariate Euclidean limit; validated against aov() for a one-way design and against the exact balanced-mixed F-test over its stratum. Controlled by mc_permutations (default 9999; set 0 to disable) and reproducible from seed. Aggregated-unit engines (random slope, unequal random intercept, unbalanced nested/hybrid) test in a reduced centroid space where the full-matrix asymptotics do not hold, so their P(MC) is left NA.

    PRIMER-style nested containment labels

    • Covariate-adjusted nested summaries now label strata with PRIMER containment notation (Site(Location), Area(Site(Location)), Residual) in the table, the denominators, and the V() variance components, derived from the design’s nesting rather than hard-coded. The estimates of components of variation are reported in a single PRIMER-style block with S() fixed-effect sizes and V() random variance components.

    Internal checkpoint label: 2.5.0.9000 (unreleased).

    Structured mixed-model denominators

    • Added structured_denominator(), a Cornfield–Tukey / Satterthwaite denominator constructor that synthesises mean squares in containment-lattice order rather than by the minimum-norm match used in quasi_denominator(). On a clean balanced design it returns the exact single-source denominator; on a perturbed (e.g. random-slope) design it returns the structured combination with Satterthwaite degrees of freedom. Validated against the clean balanced limit and against lmerTest denominator df (the latter requires the covariate to be within-centred, e.g. via decompose_covariate(), so the fixed slope’s expected mean square is not contaminated by the random intercept).

    Covariate-adjusted nested inference

    • Added permanova_nested_covariate() (and auto-routing from permanova()): categorical factors in a balanced /-generated hierarchy can now be tested while adjusting for one or more continuous covariates, matching PRIMER’s covariate handling (test the factors “above” the covariate relationship). Each factor’s numerator is adjusted for the covariate; its denominator stays the exact nested expected-mean-square stratum. The covariate is an observation-level nuisance charged to the deepest within-unit residual and tested there, so degrees of freedom partition every observation. A covariate with strong between-unit structure should be split into explicit between- and within-unit predictors. The permanova_nested() error message now names a within-unit continuous covariate as the cause instead of advising contr.sum.
    • Covariate-by-factor interactions are now tested. Writing factor * covariate in a nested design adds the homogeneity-of-slopes term (e.g. Location:Volume), tested over the residual as an observation-level term, with degrees of freedom taken from the residual. Previously such a term was silently dropped and the model collapsed to the additive one. Covariate-by- random interactions (random slopes) remain unsupported: their expected mean squares admit no exact or cleanly constructed denominator.
    • Added decompose_covariate(), a Mundlak-style helper that splits a covariate into between-unit (grouping-unit mean) and within-unit (deviation) parts, so a covariate with strong between-unit structure can be entered as two explicit predictors. The within part is a genuine observation-level covariate for permanova_nested_covariate(); the between part is a unit-level summary.

    Unified front door

    • permanova() accepts the dissimilarity on the formula’s left-hand side, permanova(bray ~ treatment + (1 | site), data), matching the vegan::adonis2() idiom; the one-sided ~ terms form with a separate distance argument still works. The assembled PERMANOVA table is exposed as $table on the result.
    • Added permanova(), a single entry point that accepts a formula (with data and distance) or a compiled permanova_design, routes it to the engine matching its random-effect provenance and balance, and returns a result that prints as a PERMANOVA table with a Factors block, denominators, and components of variation. Designs outside every supported envelope stop with a message rather than being approximated.
    • Added type = "I"|"II"|"III" to select the fixed-effect sum-of-squares partition; it is reported as not applicable for designs whose denominator is fixed by the random structure. When called with a formula, permanova() applies sum-to-zero contrasts to the fixed factors on a copy of the data, so Type III (and cross-level factor interactions) give the correct marginal hypotheses without the caller setting contrasts(). A pre-compiled design keeps whatever contrasts it was built with.
    • The PERMANOVA table shows a grand Total row only when the reported sources partition every observation degree of freedom; aggregated-unit engines (random slope, unequal random intercept, unbalanced nested/hybrid) omit it.
    • summary() of a fixed crossed/factorial model now prints the PRIMER-style expected-mean-squares, pseudo-F construction, and components-of-variation blocks. Each term’s EMS coefficient is the trace-derived tr(H Z Z') / df and its component estimate is (MS_term - MS_res) / coefficient; negative estimates are retained.
    • Type II sums of squares now respect marginality instead of rejecting a main effect contained in an interaction. A term is adjusted for every term that does not contain it (the containing interactions are excluded), giving the standard SAS/car/PRIMER “Type II (conditional)” hypothesis; factor SS match car::Anova(type = 2) to numerical tolerance. No additive refit is required.
    • Consolidated the vignette set from 24 example-indexed articles to 8 organised by design family.

    Internal checkpoint label: 2.4.0.9000 (unreleased).

    Development

    • Preserved the sealed v2.0.0 technical candidate while preparing the publication handoff and the next validated inference phase.
    • Closed Phase 23 external adversarial validation across Phases 19–25. The sealed v2.0.0 and Phase 25 artifacts matched their pinned checksums, all independent scalar/permutation references agreed to machine precision, and the confounded-strata safeguards held.
    • Added an SVD condition-ratio guard for covariate-adjusted contrasts. A numerically near-aliased fixed model now rejects with an actionable package diagnostic before the contrast projector can leak a low-level solve() error; the ratio is retained in adjusted-mean metadata.
    • Phase 25 targets child- and observation-level treatment inference in one unbalanced parent/child hierarchy with explicit unit-scale denominators and within-parent exchangeability contracts.
    • Added permanova_unbalanced_nested_lower() with automatic assignment-level detection, connected-incidence and absolute-scale span guards, exhaustive or Monte Carlo restricted residual permutations, and complete Test Specifications.
    • Extended mixed planned/pairwise contrasts and mixed global-null max-F to the same child- and observation-level unit models.
    • Added scalar GLH and direct permutation reconstruction, a pinned two-level simulation audit, adversarial failure cases, and a Pyrifos occasion vignette.
    • Phase 26 adds unbalanced treatment-by-region/site hybrid inference on equal-site-weight complete profile centroids, with additive region adjustment and region-by-exact-topology profile permutations.
    • Routed mixed planned/pairwise and weak complete-null max-F inference through the same unbalanced profile model and common region reference grid.
    • Added connected-incidence, complete-site-profile, topology-span, residual-df, zero-denominator, and non-Euclidean safeguards plus scalar and exhaustive profile reconstruction tests.
    • Phase 27 adds the narrow correlated (1 + condition | subject) model for balanced complete two-condition repeated measures.
    • Added residual-corrected random intercept–slope trace covariance estimates, optional positive-semidefinite truncation, and exhaustive whole-subject sign-flip inference under an explicit central-symmetry assumption.
    • Added paired-t-squared, scalar covariance, direct sign-flip, asymmetric-null sensitivity, semimetric, and Pyrifos early-versus-late validation.
    • Phase 28 adds permanova_pairwise_strong() for fixed one-factor all-pair complete-distribution equality hypotheses.
    • Every intersection uses a separate sample-size-preserving raw-label action within connected equality components; closed testing then provides strong FWER without assuming subset pivotality.
    • The proof excludes centroid-only nulls with unequal distributions, planned non-pairwise contrasts, dependent observations, and mixed or repeated designs. Exact reconstruction, partial-null preservation, calibration, and a Dune management vignette enforce that boundary.

    Internal checkpoint label: 2.0.0 (unreleased).

    Validated support-contract consolidation

    • Added permanova_capabilities() and SUPPORT-MATRIX.md as machine- and human-readable maps of every primary inferential engine.
    • Each registry row states its validated design envelope, estimand, denominator, permutation contract, error-control claim, and explicit exclusions; runtime design validators remain authoritative.
    • Extended deterministic and structural release gates to cover the registry, support matrix, public API, all 20 vignettes, and the complete Phase 1–22 documentation sequence.

    Internal checkpoint label: 1.8.0 (unreleased).

    Mixed-design global-null max-F inference

    • Added permanova_mixed_maxT() and permanova_mixed_maxT_pairwise() for all balanced and unbalanced mixed treatment structures already supported by the mixed-contrast engine.
    • One shared raw experimental-unit permutation stream respects whole-unit, exact-size, hierarchy-topology, block-by-size, or region strata and forms a maximum pseudo-F distribution.
    • Results explicitly claim only weak familywise error control under the complete treatment-null randomization hypothesis.
    • Added exact block enumeration, scalar unit-centroid reconstruction, non-Euclidean coverage, a 5,000-dataset weak-FWER audit, and a Pyrifos dose vignette.

    Internal checkpoint label: 1.7.0 (unreleased).

    Explicit continuous-covariate adjusted contrasts

    • Added derive_adjusted_means(), permanova_adjusted_contrasts(), and permanova_adjusted_pairwise() for full-rank fixed models containing categorical factors and ordinary numeric covariates.
    • Every continuous nuisance covariate requires an explicit finite reference value; categorical nuisance factors use declared equal-grid or observed- frequency weighting.
    • Added coefficient-space GLH checks, exhaustive direct Freedman–Lane reconstruction, non-Euclidean coverage, a pinned 500-replicate validation, and a Dune Management-by-A1 vignette.

    Internal checkpoint label: 1.6.0 (unreleased).

    Unbalanced mixed-design contrasts

    • Extended permanova_mixed_contrasts() and permanova_mixed_pairwise() to unequal random-intercept units, unbalanced top-level parent/child hierarchies, and incomplete or unequally replicated randomized blocks.
    • Cluster-size, complete-topology, and block-by-cell-size strata reuse the amended absolute-scale span guard before any contrast permutation.
    • Incomplete blocks use equally weighted observed cell centroids, an additive block model, and treatment means averaged over one common block reference grid.
    • Added scalar GLH checks for all three structures, exhaustive direct permutation reconstruction, a pinned 500-replicate audit, and an unequal- replication Pyrifos vignette.

    Internal checkpoint label: 1.5.1 (unreleased).

    Stratified-exchangeability safeguard amendment

    • Replaced relative QR rank checks in the Phase 11 and Phase 12 exchangeability-span guards with an SVD rank threshold measured absolutely relative to the original treatment-design scale.
    • Fully size-confounded, hierarchy-topology-confounded, and within-block cell-size-confounded treatments now reject before permutation instead of admitting a degenerate p-value of one.
    • Added adversarial floating-dust regression tests for all three validators; supported cluster-centroid, top-centroid, and cell-centroid references remain unchanged to machine precision.

    Internal checkpoint label: 1.5.0 (unreleased).

    Release-candidate hardening

    • Added multi-platform R CMD check CI for release R on Linux, macOS, and Windows, including dependency caching and source-package artifact upload.
    • Added a structural release audit for version/news parity, public-API/Rd parity, vignette count, S3 registration, build hygiene, and placeholder publication metadata.
    • Added release-readiness documentation separating a green technical package gate from the unresolved maintainer identity, repository URL, and bug-tracker metadata required before public submission.
    • Added deterministic release-audit tests and a bounded benchmark smoke gate.

    Internal checkpoint label: 1.4.0 (unreleased).

    Global-null max-F inference

    • Added permanova_maxT() and permanova_maxT_pairwise() for fixed one-factor planned or pairwise contrast families.
    • Every contrast uses one shared raw-observation permutation stream; adjusted p-values compare the observed pseudo-F with the permutation maximum.
    • Results explicitly label the guarantee as weak FWER under the complete equal-centroid null and do not claim strong subset-null control.
    • Added exact brute-force joint-distribution checks, non-Euclidean coverage, a 5,000-dataset family-error audit, and a Dune Management vignette.

    Internal checkpoint label: 1.3.0 (unreleased).

    Mixed-design planned contrasts

    • Added permanova_mixed_contrasts() and permanova_mixed_pairwise() for one categorical treatment in four validated balanced structures: a random intercept, a top-level nested hierarchy, a declared randomized block, and a crossed-nested region/site hybrid.
    • Contrasts operate on equally weighted cluster, top-unit, treatment-cell, or treatment-profile centroids and use the corresponding experimental-unit, treatment-by-block, or treatment-by-region residual denominator.
    • Contrast-specific Freedman–Lane residual permutations move whole units or remain within blocks/regions. Unsupported imbalance and wrong-level treatments reject explicitly.
    • Added scalar GLH references for every structure, exhaustive response-level permutation agreement, a pinned null/power validation, and a Pyrifos planned-contrast vignette.

    Internal checkpoint label: 1.2.0 (unreleased).

    Multifactor marginal contrasts

    • Added derive_marginal_means() with explicit equal-reference-grid or observed-frequency nuisance weighting for full-rank categorical fixed models.
    • Added permanova_marginal_contrasts() and permanova_marginal_pairwise() with general-linear-hypothesis projectors, contrast-specific Freedman–Lane permutations, and explicit multiplicity adjustment.
    • Continuous nuisance variables, random effects, aliased reference grids, and implicit weighting reject before inference.
    • Added scalar GLH and response-reconstruction references, a 500-replicate null/power validation, and a Dune Management-by-Use vignette.

    Internal checkpoint label: 1.1.0 (unreleased).

    Unequal-random-intercept calibration audit

    • Added audit_unequal_random_intercept_calibration() to compare exhaustive unique treatment-label assignments, Monte Carlo inference, and the complete distance engine across non-overlapping seed batches.
    • Proved and regression-tested that the intercept-only cluster-centroid Freedman–Lane transformation is algebraically identical to raw centroid permutation.
    • Added Gaussian, heavy-tail, unequal-allocation, and deliberate dispersion- violation scenarios. Only exchangeable nulls contribute to the calibration gate.
    • Distinguished all profile rearrangements from unique treatment-label assignments in Phase 11 result metadata.
    • Fixed a zero-permutation matrix-construction warning in stratified plans.
    • The 40,000-dataset audit explains the earlier elevated 500-dataset batch: valid exact rejection rates are 4.53–4.76%, with full-engine agreement to machine precision.

    Internal checkpoint label: 1.0.0 (unreleased; not the future stable release).

    Planned contrasts and pairwise post-hoc inference

    • Added permanova_contrasts() for user-specified one-df contrasts among the centroids of one categorical fixed factor with unequal group sizes.
    • Each contrast retains all orthogonal group-centroid directions as nuisance structure and receives its own Freedman–Lane residual permutation.
    • Added permanova_pairwise() to construct every pairwise centroid difference. Holm is the default adjustment; Bonferroni, BH, BY, and no adjustment are explicit alternatives.
    • Invalid/non-zero-sum contrast definitions, mixed or multifactor designs, aliases, and zero residual df reject before inference.
    • Added exact constrained-scalar references, non-Euclidean coverage, a pinned null/power validation, and a Dune planned/pairwise vignette.

    Internal checkpoint label: 0.9.0 (unreleased).

    Unbalanced nested and randomized-block inference

    • Added permanova_unbalanced_nested() for one treatment assigned to top units of an unequal parent/child hierarchy. Equally weighted top centroids exchange only among identical sorted child-count topologies.
    • Added permanova_unbalanced_block() for incomplete and/or unequally replicated randomized blocks with an explicit treatment:block component. Equally weighted intact cell centroids exchange only within block and exact cell-size strata.
    • Both engines require their restricted permutation action to span every treatment contrast and reject disconnected incidence, confounded topology, aliases, or zero residual df.
    • Added exhaustive scalar reconstructions, non-Euclidean tests, a combined operating-characteristic harness, and a Dune unbalanced-mixed vignette.

    Internal checkpoint label: 0.8.0 (unreleased).

    Unequal-replication random-intercept inference

    • Added permanova_unequal_random_intercept() for one cluster-level categorical treatment and one random intercept with unequal observations per unit.
    • The estimand is explicitly cluster weighted: the analysis uses equally weighted cluster centroids rather than silently giving larger clusters more influence.
    • Freedman–Lane residual permutations move complete cluster centroids only within exact cluster-size strata; those strata must span every treatment contrast.
    • No pooled observation-weighted EMS or parametric F distribution is claimed. Non-Euclidean empirical inference retains the complete Gower spectrum.
    • Added exhaustive scalar references, unsafe-design failures, a Pyrifos vignette, and pinned null/power validation.

    Internal checkpoint label: 0.7.0 (unreleased).

    Unbalanced fixed-effect inference

    • Added derive_unbalanced_hypotheses() and permanova_unbalanced() for explicit fully estimable Type I, II, or III fixed-effect hypotheses.
    • Type I tests are sequential; additive Type II tests are marginal and order-invariant; Type III tests retain all other terms and require a full-rank model plus explicit sum-to-zero contrasts when interactions occur.
    • Partially estimable terms, aliased incomplete Type III models, Type II main effects contained in interactions, zero residual df, and all random-effect structures reject before inference.
    • Every term uses the common full-model residual denominator and its own Freedman–Lane reduced-model residual permutation.
    • Added exact 5! enumeration, non-Euclidean empirical inference, scalar Type I/II/III references, incomplete-additive coverage, and pinned unequal- cell null/power validation.

    Internal checkpoint label: 0.6.0 (unreleased).

    Balanced crossed-nested hybrids

    • Added permanova_hybrid() for one fixed treatment crossed with regions and with sites nested within regions.
    • The exact envelope requires explicit region, region:site, treatment:region, and treatment:region:site random-intercept covariance components, complete treatment occurrence within every site, and equal residual replication.
    • Added orthogonal crossed-nested strata, trace-derived EMS, the exact MS[treatment:region] denominator, and unrestricted five-component variance estimates.
    • Exact or seeded Monte Carlo permutations move complete treatment-by-region profiles within regions, carrying every site and replicate descendant intact.
    • Added exhaustive profile-permutation references, non-Euclidean inference, strict provenance/balance failures, and pinned null/power validation.

    Internal checkpoint label: 0.5.0 (unreleased).

    Design-aware multivariate dispersion

    • Added permanova_dispersion() for one categorical fixed target in balanced one-way, single-random-intercept, nested, and canonical randomized-block designs.
    • Distances to group spatial medians are the default; centroids and the equal-group-size bias adjustment are explicit options.
    • Positive and negative principal-coordinate axes are retained. Negative squared pseudo-Euclidean distances to a center are counted, warned about, and changed to zero rather than being silently discarded.
    • Dispersion responses use the target term’s exact EMS denominator and full-model residual permutations at the correct exchangeability level.
    • One-way geometry, F statistics, and permutation vectors agree with vegan::betadisper() and permutest() under identical arrangements.
    • Added exhaustive scalar-reference checks for one-way and crossed residual permutations plus a four-structure operating-characteristic validation.
    • Improved the Phase 6 cross-level interaction diagnostic to name explicit contr.sum assignment and added an executable split-plot example.

    Internal checkpoint label: 0.4.0 (unreleased).

    Crossed randomized-block permutation inference

    • Added p_method = "permutation" to permanova_crossed() for the canonical balanced fixed-treatment × random-block model with an explicitly declared treatment-by-block random component.
    • Permutations rearrange complete replicated treatment cells within each block; no replicate separates from its cell and no cell crosses a block.
    • Added exact (treatments!)^blocks enumeration, seeded Monte Carlo sampling, attainable-space metadata, duplicate-draw reporting, and retained statistics.
    • Empirical p-values remain available for non-Euclidean dissimilarities while the complete negative spectrum is retained.
    • Added exhaustive two- and three-treatment references, direct response-level statistic comparisons, exchangeability failures, a pinned validation with dispersion sensitivity, and a randomized-block ecological vignette.

    Internal checkpoint label: 0.3.0 (unreleased).

    Level-specific balanced nested inference

    • Generalized permanova_nested() from top-level effects to fixed terms assigned at any one orthogonal level of a balanced hierarchy.
    • Region effects permute whole regions, site effects permute intact sites within regions, and observation effects permute observations within deepest units.
    • Test Specifications now record assignment level, parent level, exact level-specific EMS denominator, attainable permutation space, and the hypothesis-specific exchangeability algorithm.
    • Added exhaustive global, within-parent, and within-unit permutation tests; classical nested-ANOVA comparisons at all three levels; balanced cross-level interaction checks; and explicit rejection of level-spanning covariates.
    • Added simulate_nested_level_validation() with binomial uncertainty and per-level classical agreement diagnostics.

    Internal checkpoint label: 0.2.0 (unreleased).

    Balanced nested mixed designs

    • Added exact inference for one complete balanced /-generated random-intercept hierarchy, such as (1 | region/site), when fixed predictors are constant within top-level units.
    • Added trace-derived nested EMS, an exact residual top-unit denominator, and term-specific Freedman–Lane permutation of intact top-level hierarchies.
    • Added unrestricted nested variance-component estimates, with zero truncation available only as a separately reported sensitivity analysis.
    • Unsupported imbalance, incomplete or crossed hierarchies, random slopes, and wrong-level fixed predictors reject explicitly.
    • Added analytical ANOVA agreement, exhaustive 6! permutation coverage, three-level hierarchy checks, a 500-replicate calibration experiment, and a nested ecological-community vignette.

    Internal checkpoint label: 0.1.1 (unreleased).

    Crossed-EMS safety amendment

    • Explicit : random interactions are distinct from / nesting throughout the canonical Design Object.
    • Declared fixed-by-random interaction components enter trace-derived EMS and can provide exact classical interaction denominators.
    • Omitted fixed-by-random components now reject by default. Additive pooling requires assume_additive = TRUE and records all assumed-zero components and pooled strata.
    • Satterthwaite p-values are suppressed for non-Euclidean dissimilarities.
    • Added deterministic adversarial checks and a reproducible crossed-interaction Type I validation with binomial confidence intervals.
